businesses.business: Natural gas distribution and pipeline investment

offering_description.value: The company sells and delivers natural gas to households, businesses and industrial customers through its local gas utility. It produces renewable natural gas from wastewater biogas under a cooperative agreement. Its midstream subsidiary invests in natural gas transportation infrastructure.

quotes.quote: RGC Resources is an energy services company engaged in the sale and distribution of natural gas to approximately 64,500 residential, commercial and industrial customers in Roanoke, Virginia, and the surrounding localities, through its Roanoke Gas subsidiary. In addition to Roanoke Gas, RGC Midstream is a subsidiary that invests in natural gas transportation infrastructure including the Mountain Valley Pipeline (MVP), MVP Southgate and MVP Boost.

The Western Virginia Water Authority and Roanoke Gas Company entered into a cooperative agreement to produce commercial quality renewable natural gas, or RNG, from biogas produced at the Roanoke Regional Water Pollution Control Plant. This RNG product is the first of its kind in the Commonwealth.

regulatory_exposure.value: high: Company history documents a Roanoke gas franchise and Federal Power Commission certification for pipeline construction

quotes.quote: The Company’s franchise with the City of Roanoke, whose provisions included authorization for the City to purchase the gas property, was set to expire. The City chose to extend the franchise for another 30 years. With that, the leadership guided the Company through expansion and improvements.

Growth continued as plans were developed to bring natural gas to Roanoke. Roanoke Gas received its certificate from the Federal Power Commission and organized the Roanoke Pipe Line Company to build a 30-mile pipeline from Gala, Virginia to Roanoke. It was completed in the late summer of 1950 and natural gas was introduced to homes and businesses. New natural gas rates were 20% lower than the manufactured gas rates and the BTU content was nearly double that of manufactured gas.
